description: Tick-scaled block-parking (automatic unparking) and finalization (rolling checkpoints) vectors, mirroring validation.cpp's FindMostWorkChain and FindBlockToFinalize structures. Parking: requiredWork = tipChainWork + penalty, accepted iff the competing tip's chainwork strictly exceeds requiredWork; penalty P = D >> 3, i.e. floor(D / 8), for tickDepth < 2400 and P = D for tickDepth >= 2400, where D = tipChainWork - forkChainWork and tickDepth is the divergence depth in ticks on the defending branch's schedule. Equivalently, with E the competing branch's work since the fork, accepted iff E > D + P. The rule reads only (D, tickDepth), so the vectors carry the fork's chainwork (which cancels), the defender's span work and the competitor's span work directly, and heights only serve to derive the tick depth through a schedule. No block's work is computed and no nBits value is used. penaltyNum/penaltyDen express P as D*num/den with the quotient floored, 1/8 short of the lock-in and 1/1 at it and beyond, so they also name the arm; slackVsThreshold pins competingWorkSinceFork - (D + penalty): the vectors that sit on the threshold use 0 to reject (pinning the strict >) and 1 to accept, while vectors that deliberately sit away from it pin their margin. The lockin_flip_*, seam_flip_* pairs hold D and E fixed and change only the depth. The penalty_depth* vectors use the never-activated `empty` schedule, so they pin the penalty function only: a chain-level verdict at those depths comes from the legacy arm, which would flip penalty_depth1_accept, penalty_depth2_accept and penalty_depth3_accept. Every other parking vector has its defending tip above its schedule's entry height. A span may straddle a schedule entry, including the activation boundary, as long as H_a + 1 is part of the defending branch (height(def) >= H_a + 1); the legacy count-keyed penalty for a tip still at or below H_a (height(def) <= H_a) is out of scope here. The wide_2_255_* vectors use D = 2^255 - 1 with the fork at zero, the largest span for which tipChainWork + D does not exceed 256 bits. Finalization: candidate is the shallowest block at >= 6,000 ticks burial; the walk finalizes the candidate if now >= receiveTime + delay (inclusive) else walks back one block at a time, stopping at the already-finalized block; receiveTime 0 means disk-loaded = aged. The finalization check runs only when a new block connects (the `tip` field); the node startup grace period is a caller precondition, not a vector. Chainwork uses arith_uint256; hex fields are 64-char big-endian.

parking.name: penalty_depth1_reject
parking.note: d=600: P = D/8 = U/8 = 720,000, so E == D + P = 6,480,000 stays parked. Depth 1 is never parked (the trigger is block-count, depth >= 2), so this pins the function only

parking.name: penalty_depth1_accept
parking.note: one unit above the threshold. The legacy arm would need E > D + U/2 = 1.5U at this depth and reject, so the accept pins the penalty function only

parking.name: penalty_depth2_reject
parking.note: d=1200: P = D/8 = U/4 = 1,440,000; E == D + P stays parked

parking.name: penalty_depth2_accept
parking.note: one unit above the threshold. The legacy arm would need E > D + U/2 = 2.5U and reject, so the accept pins the penalty function only

parking.name: penalty_depth3_reject
parking.note: d=1800: P = D/8 = 3U/8 = 2,160,000, still the flat ratio: three 600-tick blocks are short of the lock-in

parking.name: penalty_depth3_accept
parking.note: one unit above the threshold. The legacy arm would need E > D + U = 4U and reject, so the accept pins the penalty function only

parking.name: penalty_depth4_reject
parking.note: d=2400: P = D, the 2x rule; E == 2D stays parked

parking.name: penalty_depth4_accept
parking.note: one unit above the threshold

parking.name: t60_depth1_reject
parking.note: d=60, one 60-tick block, D = U + 1 so D mod 8 = 1: P = floor(D/8) = 720,000 and the threshold is 6,480,001. There is no floor band: the ratio is 1/8 from the first tick. Depth 1 is never parked, so this pins the function

parking.name: t60_depth1_accept
parking.note: one unit above the threshold

parking.name: t60_depth2_reject
parking.note: d=120, the shallowest depth the trigger parks: P = D/8 = U/4 = 1,440,000, a quarter of one block's work, so two equal-height tips need 12.5% more work across the span and the depth-2 tie stays settled by work

parking.name: t60_depth2_accept
parking.note: one unit above the threshold: +12.5% per block clears it

parking.name: t60_depth7_reject
parking.note: d=420: P = 7U/8 = 5,040,000, still under one block's work, so an eighth competing block of work U (E = 8U) would clear it: the last depth at which a one-block lead suffices

parking.name: t60_depth7_accept
parking.note: one unit above the threshold

parking.name: t60_depth8_reject
parking.note: d=480, eight blocks: P = 8U/8 = U exactly, one whole block. E = 9U is a one-block lead of equal-work blocks and sits exactly on the threshold, so it stays parked: the first depth at which a one-block lead stops sufficing

parking.name: t60_depth8_accept
parking.note: one unit above the threshold

parking.name: t60_depth20_accept
parking.note: one unit above the threshold

parking.name: t60_depth30_accept
parking.note: one unit above the threshold

parking.name: t60_depth39_reject
parking.note: d=2340, the last 60-tick block short of the lock-in, with D = 39U + 7 so D mod 8 = 7: P = floor(D/8) = 28,080,000, the 7/8 of a unit floored away, not rounded up

parking.name: t60_depth39_accept
parking.note: one unit above the threshold

parking.name: t60_cap2400_reject
parking.note: d=2400, forty 60-tick blocks: P = D = 40U

parking.name: t60_cap2400_accept
parking.note: one unit above the threshold

parking.name: round_mod0_reject
parking.note: D = 16, D mod 8 = 0: P = 2 exactly, threshold 18; E == 18 stays parked

parking.name: round_mod0_accept
parking.note: E = 19 is one unit above the threshold

parking.name: round_mod1_reject
parking.note: D = 17, D mod 8 = 1: P = floor(17/8) = 2, threshold 19; a ceiling would give P = 3 and threshold 20

parking.name: round_mod1_accept
parking.note: E = 20 is accepted: 8E = 160 > 9D = 153. A ceiling (threshold 20) would keep it parked

parking.name: round_mod7_reject
parking.note: D = 23, D mod 8 = 7: P = floor(23/8) = 2, threshold 25; 8E = 200 < 9D = 207, so E == 25 stays parked

parking.name: round_mod7_accept
parking.note: E = 26 is accepted: 8E = 208 > 9D = 207. Rounding to nearest or up (P = 3, threshold 26) would keep it parked

parking.name: tiny_span_reject
parking.note: D = 7 < 8: P = 0, so the threshold is D itself; E == D still stays parked, because the comparison is strict

parking.name: tiny_span_accept
parking.note: D = 7, P = 0: E = D + 1 is accepted

parking.name: odd_span_reject
parking.note: D = 8,590,065,666, past 32 bits with D mod 8 = 2, at d = 700: P = floor(D/8) = 1,073,758,208 (remainder 2), threshold 9,663,823,874

parking.name: odd_span_accept
parking.note: one unit above the threshold

parking.name: lockin_2399_reject
parking.note: one tick short of the lock-in: still P = floor(D/8) = 720,000, threshold 6,480,001. Nothing ramps up on approach

parking.name: lockin_2399_accept
parking.note: one unit above the threshold

parking.name: lockin_2400_reject
parking.note: at the lock-in (d >= 2400 is inclusive): P = D, threshold 2D = 11,520,002

parking.name: lockin_2400_accept
parking.note: E = 2D + 1 is accepted

parking.name: lockin_2401_reject
parking.note: one tick past the lock-in: P is still exactly D

parking.name: lockin_2401_accept
parking.note: E = 2D + 1 is accepted

parking.name: lockin_flip_2399_accepted
parking.note: E = 1.5U lies strictly between D + floor(D/8) = 6,480,001 and 2D = 11,520,002: accepted at d = 2399 with 2,159,999 of slack. Same D and E as lockin_flip_2400_parked

parking.name: lockin_flip_2400_parked
parking.note: the same D and E one tick deeper: parked, 2,880,002 short of 2D. Only d changed, so this pair pins which side of 2400 the cap arm starts on

parking.name: fine1_depth1_reject
parking.note: d = 1, the smallest non-zero depth, D = U + 7: P = floor(D/8) = 720,000. The ratio does not shrink with depth

parking.name: fine1_depth1_accept
parking.note: one unit above the threshold

parking.name: seam_first_block_reject
parking.note: fork 1000, tip 1001: the first span whose defending tip is past the activation block, so the ratio applies; d = T(1001) - T(1000) = 60 and P = D/8. A tip at 1000 itself (H_a) still takes the legacy count-keyed arm and is out of scope here; that one block is what separates the two readings of the handover predicate

parking.name: seam_first_block_accept
parking.note: accept twin of seam_first_block_reject: one unit above D + D/8

parking.name: straddle_seam_reject
parking.note: fork 999, tip 1001: d = T(1001) - T(999) = 600,060 - 599,400 = 660, because block 1000 contributes 600 ticks and block 1001 contributes 60. Short of the lock-in, so P = D/8 = 720,000 at D = U, and E == D + P stays parked

parking.name: straddle_seam_accept
parking.note: one unit above the threshold

parking.name: straddle_interior_reject
parking.note: fork 998, tip 1002: d = 600,120 - 598,800 = 1,320, two blocks either side of the seam; D = 2U + 3 (D mod 8 = 3), so P = floor(D/8) = 1,440,000

parking.name: straddle_interior_accept
parking.note: one unit above the threshold

parking.name: seam_fork_minus3_reject
parking.note: fork H_a - 3, tip H_a + 1: d = 3 * 600 + 60 = 1,860, short of the lock-in although the span is four blocks deep, so the sub-cap arm applies: D = 4U + 1, P = floor(D/8) = 2,880,000. A rule keyed on a block count of four would charge the whole span here

parking.name: seam_fork_minus3_accept
parking.note: one unit above the threshold

parking.name: seam_fork_minus4_reject
parking.note: fork H_a - 4, tip H_a + 1: d = 4 * 600 + 60 = 2,460, past the lock-in, so the cap arm applies: D = 5U + 1, P = D, threshold 2D = 57,600,002

parking.name: seam_fork_minus4_accept
parking.note: E = 2D + 1 is accepted

parking.name: seam_flip_minus3_accepted
parking.note: D = 4U, E = 6U at d = 1,860: the threshold is 4.5U, so E = 1.5 D is accepted with 1.5U of slack. Same D and E as seam_flip_minus4_parked

parking.name: seam_flip_minus4_parked
parking.note: the same D and E with the fork one 600-tick block lower: d = 2,460, the threshold is 2D = 8U, and E = 6U is parked, 2U short. The spans are held equal on purpose, so only the depth separates the two verdicts

parking.name: same_count_3pct_rejected
parking.note: E/D = 1.03 per block against a 1.125 requirement: rejected, and rejected at every depth, because the ratio never falls. The slack pin is E - (D + P) = -1,094,400, i.e. 9.5% of D short of the threshold

parking.name: same_count_15pct_accepted
parking.note: E/D = 1.15 per block against a 1.125 requirement: accepted with 288,000 of slack, 2.5% of D above the threshold

parking.name: short_span2_of_depth3_reject
parking.note: defender at depth 3, competitor holds 2 blocks. The requirement is E > 9D/8, i.e. (3/2) * 9/8 = 27/16 per block: each competitor block must average 68.75% more work than the defender's

parking.name: short_span2_of_depth3_accept
parking.note: one unit above the threshold

parking.name: short_span9_of_depth10_reject
parking.note: defender at depth 10 against a 9-block competitor: E > 9D/8 is (10/9) * 9/8 = 1.25 per block, 25% more work per competitor block. d = 600 is not a boundary of the rule: the penalty is D/8 on both sides of it

parking.name: short_span9_of_depth10_accept
parking.note: one unit above the threshold

parking.name: mixed300_depth4_reject
parking.note: d = T(105) - T(101) = 61,500 - 60,300 = 1,200 on a 300-tick segment: identical penalty and verdict to t60_depth20_reject at the same tick depth on a 60-tick schedule

parking.name: mixed300_depth4_accept
parking.note: one unit above the threshold

parking.name: mixed300_straddle_2100_reject
parking.note: d = T(103) - T(98) = 60,900 - 58,800 = 2,100 = 2 * 600 + 3 * 300, five blocks deep and short of the lock-in: D = 7U + 5 (D mod 8 = 5), P = floor(D/8) = 5,040,000

parking.name: mixed300_straddle_2100_accept
parking.note: one unit above the threshold

parking.name: mixed300_straddle_2400_reject
parking.note: one 300-tick block deeper: d = 61,200 - 58,800 = 2,400, exactly the lock-in, reached in six blocks: P = D, threshold 2D = 80,640,010

parking.name: mixed300_straddle_2400_accept
parking.note: E = 2D + 1 is accepted

parking.name: wide_span_reject
parking.note: D = 1.6e19, close to 2^64: P = D/8 = 2e18 exactly and the threshold 1.8e19 still fits 64 bits, where 9 * D would not

parking.name: wide_span_accept
parking.note: one unit above the threshold

parking.name: wide_2_200_reject
parking.note: D = 2^200 + 7 (D mod 8 = 7): P = floor(D/8) = 2^197, threshold 2^200 + 2^197 + 7. The shift crosses limb boundaries and the low 7 is floored away

parking.name: wide_2_200_accept
parking.note: one unit above the threshold

parking.name: wide_2_255_sub_cap_reject
parking.note: D = 2^255 - 1 (D mod 8 = 7) on the sub-cap arm: P = 2^252 - 1, threshold 2^255 + 2^252 - 2. Shift-and-add is exact here; 9 * D would wrap 256 bits

parking.name: wide_2_255_sub_cap_accept
parking.note: one unit above the threshold

parking.name: wide_2_255_cap_reject
parking.note: D = 2^255 - 1 on the cap arm, the largest span whose 2D fits: threshold 2D = 2^256 - 2, no wrap; E == 2D stays parked

parking.name: wide_2_255_cap_accept
parking.note: E = 2D + 1 = 2^256 - 1, the largest representable chainwork, is accepted

parking.name: base_huge_reject
parking.note: same spans and depth as t60_depth2_reject with a huge base: same penalty, same verdict

parking.name: base_huge_accept
parking.note: same spans and depth as t60_depth2_accept with a huge base: the penalty is a share of the span, not of the total

parking.name: base_huge_odd_reject
parking.note: and with the base's low bit set, so the subtraction cannot be truncating anywhere
